Unification

Source: R/unify.R
unify.Rd

unify(x, y, s, variables) lists the substitutions (named lists from the variables to expressions) that make x and y equal, treating the symbols in variables as wildcards; sums, products, unions, intersections and finite sets match associatively, and commutatively where SymPy's do. rewriterule(source, target, variables, condition, assume) returns a function giving the rewrites of an expression. unify_core() is the generic algorithm on unify_compound(), unify_variable() and unify_condvariable() trees.

Usage

unify_compound(op, args)

unify_variable(arg)

unify_condvariable(arg, valid)

unify_core(x, y, s = list(), fns = list())

unify(x, y, s = list(), variables = list(), ...)

rewriterule(
  source,
  target,
  variables = list(),
  condition = NULL,
  assume = NULL
)

Arguments

op, args, arg, valid

Parts of a tree.

x, y

Expressions or trees.

s

A starting substitution.

fns

Named list with is_associative and is_commutative.

variables

Symbols that act as wildcards.

...

Unused.

source, target

Patterns.

condition

A predicate on the matched values.

assume

A boolean assumption the match must satisfy.

Value

A list of substitutions, or a rewrite function.

Examples

x <- Symbol("x"); y <- Symbol("y"); z <- Symbol("z")
unify(Symbol("a") + Symbol("b"), x + y, variables = list(x, y))
#> [[1]]
#> [[1]]$x
#> a
#> 
#> [[1]]$y
#> b
#> 
#> 
#> [[2]]
#> [[2]]$y
#> a
#> 
#> [[2]]$x
#> b
#> 
#>
